name: Switzerland
headline_status: Recreational cannabis with 1% THC or more is illegal in Switzerland, but small personal possession is not a crime, low-THC CBD flower is legal, and doctors can prescribe medical cannabis.
summary: Swiss law bans cannabis with an average THC content of 1% or more, but possessing up to 10 g for personal use is not a criminal offence and adult use can be punished with a CHF 100 fixed fine. Flower under 1% THC can be sold legally. Since 2021 the law has allowed time-limited city pilot projects selling cannabis to registered participants, and since August 2022 doctors can prescribe medical cannabis without special federal permission. A parliamentary bill to regulate adult use is still being revised in committee.

possession_limit.value: Possessing up to 10 g for personal use is not a criminal offence for adults.

penalties.value: Since 2013, adult cannabis use can be punished with a CHF 100 fixed fine; how this is applied varies by canton.

hemp_thc.value: Cannabis with less than 1% THC is outside the Narcotics Act; high-CBD flower under that limit can be legally bought and sold.

retail_sales.value: No general retail. Since May 2021 the Narcotics Act permits local, time-limited pilot projects that dispense cannabis to registered participants through pharmacies, non-profit outlets or social clubs.

medical_since.value: August 2022, when doctors could start prescribing cannabis medicines without an exceptional FOPH authorisation.

medical_program.value: Physicians prescribe directly; mandatory health insurance covers cannabis medicines only in exceptional cases.

tourists.value: Visitors have no legal way to buy THC cannabis; they can legally buy CBD flower under 1% THC, and using regular cannabis risks the CHF 100 fixed fine.

timeline.event: CHF 100 fixed fine introduced for adult cannabis use
Narcotics Act amendment allows local cannabis pilot projects
Doctors can prescribe medical cannabis without special FOPH approval
National Council health committee sends draft Cannabis Products Act back to a subcommittee for revision

pending.item: Cannabis Products Act (parliamentary initiative 20.473) would regulate adult-use sales and allow limited home growing.
pending.status: Consultation completed; in May 2026 the National Council committee referred the draft back to a subcommittee. It still needs both chambers and could face a referendum.

faq.a: No, cannabis with 1% THC or more is illegal, but possessing up to 10 g is not a crime and use usually brings at most a CHF 100 fine. CBD flower under 1% THC is legal.

faq.q: Can tourists buy cannabis in Switzerland?
faq.a: Only low-THC CBD products. City pilot projects are for registered participants, and there are no open adult-use shops.
A bill to regulate adult use is in parliament but is being revised in committee, and any final law could be put to a referendum.
